findings.description: The `merge` event used to be written right after `transitionSession(..., 'merged')`. It now runs only after the ratchet and `draftDecisionRecord`, which runs a synchronous `claude -p` that can take up to 120s. For that whole time the session reads as `merged` with no merge event, and if `saveProjectBaseline` or `draftDecisionRecord` throws, the event is never written even though the target already holds the pinned sha.

The `finally` now does fallible work: `commitsPastPin` runs `runGit rev-list`, and `appendEvent` writes to the database. If either throws, it replaces the teardown's exception and any later statements are skipped. The `deleted` flag plus the nested try/catch inside an outer try/finally is more control flow than the job needs.
The new boolean `let deleted = false;` breaks `docs/conventions/general.md` line 84: "**Boolean names** start with `is` / `has` / `should` / `can`". The rule is guidance-grade, so it caps at nit.
The JSDoc `"merged into main at <sha>": whichever of the target and the pinned sha were stored.` restates the function body, which is three lines. It also hard-codes `main` as an example.

process_issues.description: The conventions reviewer said it did not review src/core/types/session-event.types.ts or the three test files: it ran a path-scoped git diff on that file with the wrong path and got nothing back. Correctness, maintainability and docs did cover those files.
